liebermann.notes: The Red Book of the Exchequer, a collection compiled and corrected by the Exchequer official Alexander of Swereford (d. 1246), edited by Hall. Contains Leges Henrici (ff. 16–29v, c. 1225, corrected by Swereford), a tract on hides and the three law districts, financial pieces and the Dialogus de scaccario, and c. 1230 Wl art Lond retr and from the Quadripartitus Wl lad, CHn cor, Hn mon, Hn com and the Concordia of Stephen and Henry (1153). This part was copied in K3 and later Cambridge Trinity O 10, 20, the whole volume in Hg (1252); Hn was copied from it in Harley 311, Cambridge Dd VI 38 and Harley 785.

entries.text_de:
Scaccarii liber rubeus im Public Record Office zu London, eine Sammlung von Archivalien, die der Exchequerbeamte Alexander von Swereford († 1246) anlegte und corrigirte, mit werthvoller Forschung herausgegeben von Hall4.

Die jetzt zuerst stehenden f. 1—15, dort p. lxv—lxxxiv gelehrt katalogisirt, sind eingetragen erst nach f. 16, womit einst der Band begann.

F. 16—29b5 Hn, u. S. 547, um 1225 geschrieben, gleich hernach von Swereford corrigirt, erst dann von dritter gleichzeitiger Hand rubricirt6 mit den archetypen Überschriften, die z. Th. auch schon vom Schreiber in Kreide schwarz vorgeschrieben stehen.

F. 29b [M]yrcheneland est de XXX hid’ . . . To Þestsexenelaga belympeþ nygen sire, ein Tractat über die Hufenzahl der Stämme vor 10. Jh. und Englands drei Rechtsgebiete, ist in derselben Hand angefügt.

Dann folgen in anderen Händen finanzielle Statistiken, Dialogus de scaccario7 u. v. a.

Wiederum um 1230, aber in anderer Hand als Hn, f. 162b Wl art Lond retr, u. S. 489; f. 163 aus Quadr.: Wl lad, u. S. 483 und f. 163b [also zum zweiten Male] CHn cor, u. S. 521; f. 163b Hn mon, u. S. 523; f. 164 Hn com, u. S. 524; Concordia inter Stephanum et Henricum [1153]8. Dieses Stück, f. 162 ff., copirten im 15. Jh. K 3 (o. S. xxxii), sammt Hn Harley 311 und später Cambridge Trin. O 10, 20, den ganzen Band 1252 Hg (o. S. xxix). Ferner copirte Hn hieraus Cambridge Dd VI 38, Harley 785.
entries.text_en:
Scaccarii liber rubeus in the Public Record Office in London, a collection of records which the Exchequer official Alexander of Swereford († 1246) compiled and corrected, edited with valuable research by Hall4.

The f. 1—15 that now stand first, learnedly catalogued there, pp. lxv—lxxxiv, were entered only after f. 16, with which the volume once began.

F. 16—29b5 Hn, below, p. 547, written c. 1225, corrected immediately afterwards by Swereford, only then rubricated6 by a third contemporary hand with the archetypal headings, which in part also already stand pre-written by the scribe in black chalk.

F. 29b [M]yrcheneland est de XXX hid’ . . . To Þestsexenelaga belympeþ nygen sire, a tract on the hidage of the peoples before the 10th century and England's three legal provinces, is added in the same hand.

Then follow in other hands financial statistics, Dialogus de scaccario7 and much else.

Again c. 1230, but in a different hand from Hn, f. 162b Wl art Lond retr, below, p. 489; f. 163 from Quadr.: Wl lad, below, p. 483 and f. 163b [thus for the second time] CHn cor, below, p. 521; f. 163b Hn mon, below, p. 523; f. 164 Hn com, below, p. 524; Concordia inter Stephanum et Henricum [1153]8. This piece, f. 162 ff., was copied in the 15th century by K 3 (above, p. xxxii), together with Hn Harley 311, and later by Cambridge Trin. O 10, 20; the whole volume by Hg in 1252 (above, p. xxix). Further, Hn was copied from this by Cambridge Dd VI 38, Harley 785.

notes.text_de: The Red book of the Exchequer (Rolls series) 1896. Vgl. mein Über Leges Henrici S. 8. Frühere Literatur: Cooper Account on the Public records II 309; Hunter Three catalogues p. 7. 33; Report of the Commissioners on the Public records 1837, p. 169. 172.
notes.text_en: The Red book of the Exchequer (Rolls series) 1896. Cf. my Über Leges Henrici p. 8. Earlier literature: Cooper Account on the Public records II 309; Hunter Three catalogues pp. 7. 33; Report of the Commissioners on the Public records 1837, pp. 169. 172.

notes.text_de: Es ist 21 und XXI, also eine Zahl zweimal, foliirt.
notes.text_en: It is foliated 21 and XXI, i.e. one number twice.

notes.text_de: Vor C. 6 bricht Rubricator eine Zeile ab, um das vom Corrector bedeckte Zeilenstück zu umgehen.
notes.text_en: Before c. 6 the rubricator breaks off a line, in order to avoid the part of the line covered by the corrector.

notes.text_de: vgl. Edition durch Hughes, Crump and Johnson p. 3.
notes.text_en: cf. the edition by Hughes, Crump and Johnson p. 3.

notes.text_de: vgl. Hall p. xcviii und Spelman hinter Wilkins’ Leges-Anglosax. 318.
notes.text_en: cf. Hall p. xcviii and Spelman at the end of Wilkins’ Leges-Anglosax. 318.

transcription.doubts: The OE incipit's initial is printed as Þ/Ƿ-like capital 'Þestsexenelaga' (the print has a thorn-shaped letter, presumably for wynn: Westsexena laga); transcribed Þ. 'hid’' has an apostrophe-like abbreviation mark. lxv—lxxxiv, xxxii, xxix, xcviii are small capitals. 'vor' (text) and 'Vor' (n. 6) are letter-spaced for emphasis. The entry runs from col. 1 foot into col. 2.
